newsitem.title: CHINA: CHANG'AN H1 SALES UP 36 PCT - NEWSPAPER.
newsitem.headline: CHANG'AN H1 SALES UP 36 PCT - NEWSPAPER.

text.p: Sales of China's Chongqing Chang'an Automobile Co Ltd rose a year-on-year 36 percent to 1.412 billion yuan in the first six months of 1997, the Beijing-based Market Daily said on Friday.
Chang'an produced 60,900 cars in first six months, up 80.9 percent from the year-earlier period, the newspaper said without saying how many cars were sold.
Earnings rose 14 percent, it said. It did not give a profit figure or specify whether the earnings were after taxation.
It also did not say whether the figures were using international or Chinese accounting standards.
The company, one of China's leading mini sedan car makers, posted net profit of 82.628 million yuan on sales of 1.085 billion yuan in the first half of 1996 under international accounting standards.
The company's 1996 interim results using Chinese standards were not available.
Chang'an, based in the southwestern industrial city of Chongqing, has not released its 1997 interim results to the public.
Qingling Motors Co Ltd, also based in Chongqing, turned out 15,000 automobiles in the first five months of this year, it said without giving further details.
